title: After Four-Year Search, Sanjay Govil Advances Cricket Stadium Plans in Maryland
excerpt: The Indian-American tech entrepreneur's Washington Freedom franchise has secured key approvals for a 10,000-capacity venue in Frederick, moving professional cricket closer to a permanent home in the D.C. region.
body:
• Indian-American tech entrepreneur Sanjay Govil's Washington Freedom cricket team has advanced plans for a 10,000-capacity stadium in Frederick, Maryland, after years of searching for a venue.
  • The proposed Frederick Gateway project would be built on 24 acres beside the Monocacy River, fully privately funded with no local or state tax dollars.
  • The Frederick City Council was set to vote on the proposal in August 2026, following a rezoning approval by Frederick County Council in July 2025.
  • The stadium would host Major League Cricket matches and community events, with cricket set to debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

A Four-Year Search Nears Its End

Indian-American entrepreneur Sanjay Govil, owner of Major League Cricket's Washington Freedom franchise, has secured critical approvals to build a dedicated cricket stadium in Frederick, Maryland — the culmination of a four-year search for a permanent home for professional cricket in the Washington, D.C. region.

The proposed Frederick Gateway project envisions a 10,000-capacity venue on roughly 24 acres at 8400 East Patrick Street, beside the Monocacy River near Interstate 70. The facility would feature approximately 5,000 fixed seats and room for another 5,000 spectators on grass berms, according to planning documents filed with Frederick city officials.

"It was an exhaustive process. First of all, in a country like the US, you don't know where to start for a cricket stadium. There's a lot of red tape."

— Sanjay Govil, Washington Freedom owner

From George Mason to Frederick

Govil's journey to find a stadium site has been marked by setbacks. The tech entrepreneur — founder and chairman of Infinite Computer Solutions and CEO of Zyter — first partnered with George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, in 2023 to explore building a joint cricket and baseball facility on the university's campus.

That plan collapsed in March 2024 after widespread community pushback over transparency, parking, environmental reviews, and the use of tax-exempt land. GMU President Gregory Washington confirmed the university would cease negotiations, stating the project "does not meet the strategic objectives and interests of our campus and community."

Govil's company, AcersInfra LLC, then pivoted to Frederick, proposing the Frederick Gateway project on the site of a former I-70 golf driving range. The Frederick County Council approved rezoning for the site in July 2025, transitioning the land from agricultural to recreational and commercial use.

Private Funding, Public Scrutiny

A central feature of the Frederick proposal is that construction and operation would be entirely privately financed, with no local or state tax dollars involved — a point the Washington Freedom organization has emphasized to distinguish itself from typical sports franchise stadium deals. The owner would also cover on-site infrastructure costs, according to city planning materials.

The proposal includes riverfront open space with walking trails, a boat launch, multi-purpose green space, and dedicated nature areas, positioning it as a community park as much as a sports venue.

However, the project has faced scrutiny. Frederick residents have raised concerns about traffic congestion, parking on residential streets, environmental impacts near the Monocacy River floodplain, and the venue's proximity to Frederick Municipal Airport. The city staff has required a detailed Events Management Plan covering shuttle logistics, parking, and crowd control.

Cricket's American Moment

The stadium push comes as cricket experiences a surge of interest in the United States. Major League Cricket launched its inaugural season in 2023, and cricket will make its Olympic debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games — a landmark moment for the sport in America.

Govil, who also owns a 50% stake in the Cardiff-based Welsh Fire cricket team, has been a founding investor in MLC. He told Cricbuzz he spent $500,000 of personal funds and 14 months searching for a viable stadium location in the D.C. metro area.

The proposed venue would host approximately 10 to 15 professional matches during a four-to-six-week summer window, with additional community and cricket programming extending use throughout the year. The playing field would meet International Cricket Council standards, making it eligible to host international competition.

The D.C. region, home to one of the largest South Asian populations in the United States, represents a natural market for professional cricket. If the Frederick stadium moves forward, it would become one of the first purpose-built professional cricket venues on the East Coast.
